title: introduce-hybrid-quantization-windowing-and-tenant-cost-automation
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce unit inference cost for variable workloads by introducing a tenant-aware hybrid quantization schedule and a sliding 'cost window' that couples prefill/caching defaults to short-term demand signals. This PR implements the autosuggest and enforcement pieces so tenants get safe, reversible quant and cache defaults without manual tuning.

Summary of changes: adds a hybrid quant scheduler that can apply mixed int8/int4 profiles per-tenant during low-cost windows; introduces a cost_window manager that computes short-term demand percentile (p50/p95) and proposes cache TTL and batching presets; exposes a CLI dry-run (--preview) and an API endpoint for previewing suggested defaults; integrates rollout gating via feature-flag + canary tenants; adds end-to-end smoke tests and telemetry for unit-econ impact.

Design notes: the hybrid quant scheduler maintains a compatibility matrix for model variants and uses a safety score (based on eval regression thresholds) before recommending a more aggressive quant step. The cost_window manager aggregates 1m windowed metrics (qps, avg latency, tokens/sec) and estimates marginal cost delta if the tenant moves to suggested presets. Recommendations include: batch_shape, cache_prefill_ttl, quant_profile, fallback_profile, and staging_window_seconds. All recommendations are returned as a single suggested_profile blob for simplicity.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag feature.hybrid_quant_windowing=false by default. 2) Enable for internal canary tenants (tenant ids listed in REDWOOD_CANARIES) for 48h. 3) Run econ-sim dry-run (CLI) against canary traffic to validate <=2% quality regression and >=6% cost reduction target. 4) Gradually enable with 10/30/100% tenant cohorts and automated rollback if quality/regression alerts fire.

Safety and fallback: fallback_profile keeps original model variant and cache TTL; scheduler supports immediate rollback and rolling reconfiguration without losing KV cache state. A hard SLI guard is enforced during staged rollout: if p99 latency increases by >10% or quality delta exceeds 2% BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent metric for tenant evalset, the system auto-reverts recommendations for that tenant and notifies SRE and the author.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the compatibility matrix loader (hybrid_quant/compat.go) and the new telemetry tags (telemetry/labels.go) used to correlate "suggested_profile" with unit_econ traces. The CLI (tools/econ-sim) supports --preview and --apply flags; --apply is gated.

Backwards compatibility: config defaults remain unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled per-tenant. Admins can opt-out at tenant level.

Related work: builds on previous prefill/autotune pieces (ENG-3987) and the prefilling telemetry refactor in ENG-4609.

Testing: added unit tests for scheduler heuristics, integration tests for the preview API, and a small-scale canary simulation in tools/econ-sim/sim_test.go.

Release notes: new opt-in feature for tenant-aware hybrid quantization and automated cost-window presets. Admins can preview suggestions before applying.
